El Gran Tapou (3.151 m) es la cima más a: The Gran Tapou (3,151 m) is the highest summit of the southern extension of the Vignemale massif, above the Ossoue valley, on the border between Aragon and France. Info based on a route published on Wikiloc; it has no route on the map.

You go round the Pic Rond and the Pic Pointu to the Montferrat lakes and follow cairns to Pico del Medio and the Gran Tapou. Up to there you only need your hands on one slightly exposed step. The two points of the Tapou are another matter: down-climbing, exposed scrambling, a steep snowy gully and a short abseil on the way back.

On the second day you climb the Gías ravine to the Gías tarn and up to the gap between Pico Jean Arlaud and Gourgs Blancs by an easy scrambling gully (II). From there you follow the Gourgs Blancs ridge, a chaos of granite boulders, to the Torre Armengaud and the Punta Lourde Rocheblave; then you cross to the Puerto de Gías, to the three Clarabide summits along a cairned shoulder and to Pico de Gías, with a I+ scramble. El pico Gramatuero (en occitano Pic d'Ar: Pico Gramatuero (in Occitan Pic d'Arratilha, in French Grand Pic d'Arratille, in Spanish Pico Bramatuero) is a peak 2,898 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Pandicosa and Torla (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania).

La punta d'es Ibons (en francés Mont Arr: The Punta d'es Ibons (in French Mont Arrouy, in Spanish Punta de los Ibones) is a peak 2,888 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Gèdre (Occitania).
Collarada es un pico del Pirineo aragoné: Collarada is a peak of the Aragonese Pyrenees, 2,886 m above sea level, in the municipality of Villanúa (Huesca, Spain). It is the highest point of the Jacetania comarca and one of the most striking summits in the Pyrenees because it can be seen from so far away. It lies within what geologists call the inner ranges of the Pyrenees and is part of the Ip cirque, at whose centre lies the tarn (glacial lake) of the same name.

El pico de la Capilla (en francés Pic Bl: The Pico de la Capilla (in French Pic Blanc, in Spanish Pico de la Capilla) is a peak 2,826 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Gèdre (Occitania).
El pico de Tuca Roya (en francés Pic de: The Pico de Tuca Roya (in French Pic de Tuquerouye, in Spanish Pico de Tucarroya) is a peak 2,818 metres high in the Pre-Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Gèdre (Occitania). La punta de la Meseta (en francés Pic de: The Punta de la Meseta (in French Pic de Gabiédou) is a peak 2,808 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Gèdre (Occitania).

La Pala d'Ip es una tuca pirenaica situa: The Pala d'Ip is a Pyrenean summit on the border between the Izas and Ip valleys. It has a double summit, at 2,779 and 2,775 metres. The normal route starts in Canfranc or at the Coll de Ladrones fort: it is an easy route, although very long because of its great height gain, which means it can also be climbed in winter.
La tuca Blanca es un pico de 2.766 metro: The Tuca Blanca is a peak 2,766 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Torla (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania).
El pico Larré (en francés Pic Falisse, e: Pico Larré (in French Pic Falisse, in Spanish El Yarre) is a peak 2,763 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Pandicosa (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania). It lies between the Falisse col (2,699 m) and the Marcadau pass (2,541 m); at its feet are the Pecico tarns.
El pico Partaniello (en francés Grand Pi: Pico Partaniello (in French Grand Pic de Péterneille) is a peak 2,751 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Pandicosa (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania).
La Peña Telera es un pico que forma part: Peña Telera is a peak in the Pyrenean Sierra de la Partacua, a mountain chain separating the Tena valley from the Tierra de Biescas in the Alto Gállego comarca (Huesca). It rises to 2,764 m above sea level and has a notable prominence, especially on its south face, where the drop is almost 2,000 metres. Together with the rest of the Partacua and the neighbouring Sierra Tendeñera, Peña Telera forms a natural wall that isolates the Tena valley climatically. North of this range temperatures are lower and rainfall noticeably higher.
El pico de las Oletas (en francés Pic de: The Pico de las Oletas (in French Pic des Oulettes or Pic des Mulets) is a peak 2,757 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Torla (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania).
La punta Escarra es una cima pirenaica s: The Punta Escarra is a Pyrenean summit between the Tena and Izas valleys and the Ip cirque, next to the Pala d'Ip. It is a tripoint of the municipalities of Sallent de Gállego, Canfranc and Samianigo. At 2,748 m, it is the fourth highest summit of the Ip cirque, after Collarada, the Pala d'Ip and the Pala de Alcañiz.
La tuca Salvaguardia o tuca Cabellut (en: The Tuca Salvaguardia or Tuca Cabellut (in Occitan Sauvagarda, in French Pic de Sauveguarde, in Spanish Pico Salvaguardia) is a peak 2,736 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Benasque (Aragon) and Banyeres de Luchon (Occitania).
La punta de la Muga, punta de la Güega,: The Punta de la Muga, Punta de la Güega, Pico de Marcadau Sur or Muga Sur de Marcadau (in French Muga Sud) is a peak 2,728 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Pandicosa (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania). El pico de la Pala (en francés Pic de Bo: The Pico de la Pala (in French Pic de Bounèu) is a peak 2,723 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Gèdre (Occitania).
El pico del Puerto Viello (en francés Pi: The Pico del Puerto Viello (in French Pic du Port Vieux) is a peak 2,721 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Aragnouet (Occitania).
El pico del Ratillo (en francés Les Pics: The Pico del Ratillo (in French Les Pics Jumeaux) is a peak 2,716 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Pandicosa (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania). It is really made up of two small peaks, with hardly any height difference between them, that can barely be told apart from a distance.
La punta del Garién (en castellano pico: The Punta del Garién (in Spanish Pico del Forcarral) is a peak 2,720 metres high in the Pre-Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Gèdre (Occitania).
La cima de Batcrabera (en francés Sommet: The Cima de Batcrabera (in French Sommet de Batcrabère) is a peak 2,707 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Sallent de Gállego (Aragon) and Arrens-Marsous (Occitania).
La tuca de la Mina (en francés pic de la: The Tuca de la Mina (in French Pic de la Mine) is a peak 2,708 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Benasque (Aragon) and Bagnères-de-Luchon (Occitania).
La punta Baja de las Blancas, o punta Ba: The Punta Baja de las Blancas, or Punta Baja de las Blancas de la Larri (in French Hèche de Bounèu), is a peak 2,702 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Gèdre (Occitania).
La punta de los Ibones de Pecico (en cas: The Punta de los Ibones de Pecico (in Spanish Pico de los Ibones de Pecico) is a mountain 2,704 metres high in the municipality of Pandicosa, in the Alto Gállego.
El pico Né es un pico de 2.696 metros de: Pico Né is a peak 2,696 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Torla (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania).

El pico de la Plana de l'Alba (en francé: The Pico de la Plana de l'Alba (in French Pic de Pla d'Aube) is a peak 2,678 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Torla (Aragon) and Gavarnie (Occitania).
El pico de Marcadau Norte o Muga Norte d: The Pico de Marcadau Norte or Muga Norte de Marcadau (in French Muga Nord) is a peak 2,676 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Pandicosa (Aragon) and Cauterets (Occitania).
La punta de Salcorz es un pico de 2.675: The Punta de Salcorz is a peak 2,675 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Aragnouet (Occitania).
La Peña Castillón (en francés Pène de Mi: Peña Castillón (in French Pène de Millarioux) is a peak 2,658 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Chistén (Aragon) and Saint-Lary (Occitania).
La punta Batalienza (en francés Pic de B: The Punta Batalienza (in French Pic de Bataillence) is a peak 2,604 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Aragnouet (Occitania).
El pico de ro Cardal (en francés Pic du: The Pico de ro Cardal (in French Pic du Cardal) is a peak 2,572 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Torla (Aragon) and Gavarnie (Occitania). It is in the Sierra de Sandaruelo.

La punta de l'Agulleta (en francés Pic d: The Punta de l'Agulleta (in French Pic de l'Aiguillette) is a peak 2,508 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Bielsa (Aragon) and Aragnouet (Occitania).
El pico del Puerto (en francés Pic Entre: The Pico del Puerto (in French Pic Entre les Ports) is a peak 2,476 metres high in the Pyrenees, on the border between the municipalities of Torla (Aragon) and Gavarnie (Occitania). At its feet lies the Lapazosa tarn.
El pico de Guara (Tozal de Guara en arag: The Pico de Guara (Tozal de Guara in Aragonese) is a 2,077 m mountain in the Sierra de Guara. It belongs to the Sierra y Cañones de Guara natural park and can be seen from the city of Huesca. Its height contrasts with the nearby river Alcanadre, whose lowest point is at 430 m. It is the most important spur of the Aragonese Pre-Pyrenees and lies on several hiking routes.
El llamado «Salto de Roldán» es una form: The so-called «Salto de Roldán» (Roland's Leap) is a rock formation in the Pre-Pyrenees of Huesca, in Upper Aragon. It is made up of two huge rock masses that form the gateway to the Sierra de Guara and jut out like ships' bows over the Hoya de Huesca. They are the San Miguel crag (left), 1,123 m, and the Amán crag, 1,124 m, with the river Flumen running between them. In the middle of the Tertiary period, rivers carried gravel and pebbles from the Pyrenees down to the Ebro basin. These deposits, hardened into conglomerate, have been carved by the rivers into column-like shapes called «mallos».
La sierra de Gratal es una cadena montañ: The Sierra de Gratal is an Aragonese mountain range in the first foothills of the Pyrenees, running from west to east. It lies north of the city of Huesca. One of its main heights, a survey point, is the Peña Gratal, in the middle of the range, 1,543 m high. The highest point is the Pico de la Calma, on the north side of the range above the Arguis reservoir, 1,581 m high. On the south side, the Pico Gratal, 1,567 m, is the second highest point of the range.
El Turbón es un macizo de los Pirineos,: The Turbón is a massif of the Pyrenees, in the Ribagorza district, province of Huesca, with its summit at 2,492 m. It runs from north to south, overlooking the Isábena basin to the east and the Campo depression, in the Ésera basin, to the west. It is a large anticline faulted on its eastern flank, shaped mainly in marls and thick Cretaceous limestone beds that form vertical cliffs more than 500 m high. Its flora, rich in endemic species, is of great botanical interest.
La Peña Montañesa es el nombre que recib: Peña Montañesa is the name of the highest part of the Sierra Ferrera, in the Sobrarbe district of Huesca, Spain. The name is often used for the whole range it belongs to. It lies, among others, in the municipalities of Laspuña and El Pueyo de Araguás, from where its impressive walls can be seen perfectly. The name refers to the structure of the range, made mostly of a large sedimentary limestone formation, deeply eroded by karst, which exposes a very high wall, visible from many angles in the district and around it thanks to its great prominence.
Cotiella es un macizo calcáreo del Prepi: Cotiella is a limestone massif of the Aragonese Pre-Pyrenees. The same name is given to the main peak of the massif, 2,912 m high. Other important summits are the Punta de Armeña (2,822 m), the Punta de las Neiss (2,751 m) and the Cotielleta (2,731 m). Although it does not reach 3,000 m, the relative isolation of the Cotiella makes it look like the giant of the area, with wide views from its summit. It lies between the rivers Cinca and Ésera.
La sierra de Sevil es una elevación del: The Sierra de Sevil is a range in the north-east of the Iberian Peninsula, in the province of Huesca. It is surrounded by the rivers Vero and Isuela.
Da nombre a toda la sierra y se ve desde: It gives its name to the whole range and can be seen from the city of Huesca. Between its summit and the river Alcanadre, which flows nearby at about 430 m, there is a drop of more than 1,600 m.
En lo alto están las ruinas del castillo: On top are the ruins of the castle of Sen, a Muslim fortress mentioned as early as the 10th century: remains of two towers, two large cisterns, a small church and houses. King García Sánchez I of Pamplona took it in 941 and the Muslim lord of Zaragoza won it back the following year.
Cuenta la leyenda que Roldán, el caballe: Legend has it that Roland, Charlemagne's knight, was surrounded on this crag and leapt on his horse across the abyss to the San Miguel crag, leaving his hoofprints in the rock. On top stood the Muslim stronghold of Men, the twin of the castle of Sen.
Según la tradición de la zona, aquí emba: Local tradition says Noah's Ark ran aground here: Noah is said to have exclaimed «Ya turba l'arca» («the ark is running aground» in Aragonese), which would explain the name. A saying goes: «When there is fog on the Turbón, there is rain all over Aragon».
A sus pies están las ruinas del monaster: At its foot lie the ruins of the monastery of San Victorián, documented since the 10th century and very important in the county of Sobrarbe. The crag is part of a large limestone thrust sheet that moved about 40 km.
En el macizo está el ibón de Plan o Basa: The massif holds the Plan tarn, or Basa de la Mora: tradition says that on Midsummer night a Moorish princess appears there to the pure of heart. On clear days the Cotiella can be seen from the city of Lleida.
El punto más alto de la sierra es el Pic: The highest point of the range is the Pico de la Calma (1,581 m), above the Arguis reservoir; the Peña Gratal (1,543 m), in the middle, is a survey point.
Su nombre viene de Sevil, un pueblo del: Its name comes from Sevil, a village in the municipality of Adahuesca that was already abandoned by the mid-19th century.
Es el punto más alto del municipio de Ar: It is the highest point of the municipality of Arguis. Below it to the west lies the Arguis reservoir, the oldest in Aragon.

Sendero S-9 (Salto de Roldán – Peña San: Trail S-9 (Salto de Roldán – Peña San Miguel), part of the Aragon Natural Network. It starts at the car park reached by a paved track of about 2 km, which leaves the road 500 m before Santa Eulalia de la Peña. It climbs the slope to the vertical section, where iron rungs, staples and a cable lead up to the summit plateau. The official leaflet rates it as difficult; anyone prone to vertigo should take care. There is a risk of falling rocks: do not climb in the rain.

La subida más clásica del parque natural: The most classic ascent in the natural park (trail S-5 of the Aragón Natural Network). From Santa Cilia de Panzano (743 m): a track towards the cemetery and, on a path, the hut and the Fondarrés ponds (1,538 m); then the Vallemona col (1,812 m) and the ridge to the summit. It can also be climbed from Nocito (922 m) up the Pillera ravine and the Petreñales col (1,558 m), from where a waymarked path goes round the summit on the right. No technical difficulty, but long and with no reliable water.

Desde Santa Cilia de Panzano por el mism: From Santa Cilia de Panzano on the same path as to Tozal de Guara until past the Fondarrés ponds; at the turn-off to the Cubilars col, a path on the right leads to the summit, easy to spot by its antennas.
También se le llama Tozal de los Buitres: It is also called Tozal de los Buitres (Vultures' Peak). The antennas on its summit can be seen from much of the Somontano.
Se alza junto al collado de Vallemona (1: It rises beside the Vallemona col (1,812 m), on the path from Santa Cilia de Panzano to Tozal de Guara: from the col you climb to the summit with no marked path.
Se suele subir desde Pedruel, en una cir: It is usually climbed from Pedruel, on a loop that crosses the summit and the abandoned village of Bara.
Desde el puente de Lúsera, cerca de Bels: From the Lúsera bridge, near Belsué, the most direct ascent goes up the north face. A loop links Punta Sur, Gabardiella and Pico de Luna and descends via the Luna and Paúles cols to the Belsué dam; its descents are technical.
Da nombre a la sierra de Gabardiella, el: It gives its name to the Gabardiella range, the western end of the natural park. From the summit you can see the Pyrenees and the Hoya de Huesca.
Se sube en la circular de la Gabardiella: It is climbed on the Gabardiella loop from the Lúsera bridge (Belsué): after Gabardiella you follow the ridge to Pico de Luna and descend via the Luna and Paúles cols. Technical descents.
Desde Arguis (Centro de Interpretación o: From Arguis (visitor centre or reservoir) by track and path to the summit, crowned with antennas. No technical difficulty. It can also be reached by car on the service track from the Monrepós pass.
